core_obligations: Write the space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, note that T may be viewed as a closed subset of every stage because the reductions agree, and apply the affine case of the completion statement to each stage (proof lines 7978-7985).
Show that the transition morphisms between the completions are closed immersions, as base changes of the transition morphisms of the presentation (proof lines 7985-7989).
Show that they induce isomorphisms on reductions, by the statement on reductions of completions (proof lines 7989-7992).
Identify the completion functor with the colimit of the completions of the stages and conclude by the directed colimit statement (proof lines 7992-7994).
proof_roadmap: Completions of the stages are affine (proof lines 7978-7985).
The transition morphisms are closed immersions with isomorphic reductions (proof lines 7985-7992).
Conclusion by the directed colimit statement (proof lines 7992-7994).
difficulty_reason: For an affine formal algebraic space X over a scheme and a closed subset T of its reduction, the lemma asserts that the functor of morphisms into X whose image lies in T is an affine formal algebraic space (statement lines 7968-7976). The proof writes X as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, notes that all stages have the same reduction so that T may be viewed as a closed subset of each stage, and applies the affine case of the completion statement to each stage, obtaining an affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 7978-7985). It then checks the two hypotheses of the statement on directed colimits of affine formal algebraic spaces: the transition morphisms between the completions are closed immersions because they are base changes of the transition morphisms of the presentation, and they induce isomorphisms on reductions by the corresponding statement about reductions of completions (proof lines 7985-7992). Since the completion functor is the colimit of the completions of the stages, the conclusion follows (proof lines 7992-7994). The claim is H2: the argument identifies the relevant system, verifies the two conditions under which a directed colimit of affine formal algebraic spaces is affine, and applies the affine case stage by stage.
